title: Dangermond Preserve — Creek Water Outlines (m3-v2, channel ribbon on the raw lidar bed, for m3-v2, m4-v1 and m5-v1) — exact ribbon outlines
snippet: The water outlines of WSE polygons m3-v2 exactly as computed, one row per Creek Segment and water depth, as text, for the Creek Water Visualization browser. Shown by default in the Creek Water Visualization.
description:
What this is
The same water outlines as the companion WSE polygons layer (m3-v2), stored exactly as computed: one row per creek stretch and water depth, with the outline as text. When the layer was published, the map server split outlines that cross themselves (where a ribbon folds at a bend) into simple pieces. The Creek Water Visualization reads this table instead, so it can draw each ribbon in its original order along the creek.

Accuracy and limits
These are estimates, not measurements. The stream flows are modeled without gauge correction and may be off by a factor of 2 to 5, so the timing of rises and falls is more reliable than the heights. The water depth assumes steady flow over a bare-earth lidar terrain that cannot see the underwater channel bed. Use them for research and visualization.

Service
https://dangermondpreserve-spatial.com/server/rest/services/Hosted/creek_water_visualization_wse_polygons_m3_v2_rings/FeatureServer

Technical details

Dangermond Preserve — Creek Water Outlines (m3-v2, channel ribbon on the raw lidar bed, for m3-v2, m4-v1 and m5-v1) — exact ribbon outlines. A table that goes with the hosted feature layer https://dangermondpreserve-spatial.com/server/rest/services/Hosted/creek_water_visualization_wse_polygons_m3_v2/FeatureServer.

Why it exists: Exact station-ordered rings of every depth bucket of the channel ribbon, because the published polygon layer's self-crossing rings were split by ArcGIS on publishing. The hosted browser reads this table instead of the polygon layer geometry; the polygon layer stays the version's map layer.

Columns: segment_id: Creek Segment id; tnc_comid: TNC flowline COMID (text); bucket_index: depth rung, as bucket_index in the polygon layer; min_depth_m: bucket lower bound, water depth in meters (minWaterSurfaceElevationM in the Stage 4 file); max_depth_m: bucket upper bound, water depth in meters; vertex_count: vertices in ring_json; ring_json: the bucket's one ring as [[lon, lat, bed elevation m NAVD88], …], EPSG:4326, exactly as Stage 4 wrote it; no closing vertex; left edge stations 0…n−1, then right edge n−1…0.

Provenance: frozen 2026-10-28T16:06:17Z from commit ca9d1a964f5d4f1fea63db19af9108073ecefbc2, from the same Stage 4 files as m3-v2 (SHA-256 checked); every ring equals the frozen file geodatabase geometry ({"exact": 63005, "rotated": 0, "reversed": 360}; reversed rings are the file geodatabase writer's, this table keeps the Stage 4 order).

Versioning: append-only; earlier versions are never overwritten or deleted.
accessInformation: NOAA National Water Model v3.0 retrospective; California Natural Flows Database; USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) 1 m terrain; TNC (The Nature Conservancy) flowlines; EPA NHDPlusV2. Derived by the UCSB Spatial Center.
licenseInfo: Research and visualization use. Modeled values are not validated at every creek; see the description.
